themes.name: The minimal kernel and its primitives
themes.about: What the few founding elements of the language are, from which everything else is built.

themes.name: Code as data and the self-interpreter
themes.about: Homoiconicity, Term as a datum, eval, and Luthier operating on its own code.

themes.name: Types as propositions that carry their laws
themes.about: A type states the law its values satisfy, making type safety a consequence of semantic clarity.

themes.name: The construction pattern: certified subtype and Library
themes.about: Deriving a certified type, its validating constructor and its forgetful projection from a material type and a predicate.

themes.name: Laws as predicates and verification by test
themes.about: Defining a function defines its test; laws are ordinary declarations, holes until checked.

themes.name: Generators and the quality of the sample
themes.about: How values of a type are produced for testing and what each certificate's reach then means.

themes.name: Path equivalence, implementations and optimization
themes.about: Many implementations of one function, their equivalence, and choosing the best for a case.

themes.name: The run database and its synthesis
themes.about: Recording measured time and precision per run, generalizing it, and keeping it from growing monstrous.

themes.name: The forget functor and the typing-load problem
themes.about: Controlling the typing information that grows as types compose; forgetting as a projection that defines the language.

themes.name: The external world, extern and orchestration
themes.about: The read/write boundary to C++, Python and resources, and how Luthier delegates execution.

themes.name: Probability, Bayes and statistical verification
themes.about: Marrying types with probability: laws with costs, posteriors over behavior, and verification as a Bayesian observer.

themes.name: Errors as data and the certificate
themes.about: Failure as a predicate that fails, structured error trees, and the certificate as composable graded evidence.

themes.name: Numbers: Real, Float64 and intervals
themes.about: Writing numeric code over the ideal reals and realizing it in approximations with a stated law.

themes.name: Environment, variables and memory
themes.about: The early model of an environment that stores and retrieves variables by name.

themes.name: Program as DAG, commutativity and time
themes.about: A program as an unordered set of definitions where temporality emerges from dependency.

themes.name: Concrete syntax and notation
themes.about: The surface forms: binders, symbols versus keywords, the dot, quotes, and reading the language aloud.

themes.name: Working method and the pipeline
themes.about: How the work is organized: audios to ideas to spec, records, reviews, waterfall versus iteration, mechanical checks.

themes.name: The derivation store and provenance
themes.about: Storing derived objects as proof terms with their inputs, never edited, cumulative.

themes.name: Mathematical structures, presentations and translations
themes.about: Expressing algebraic objects as types with laws, their several presentations, and certified translations between them.

themes.name: Sonolocalización: the inference application
themes.about: The concrete case that drives Luthier: situated objects, MAP, likelihood, score identities and the sampler.

themes.name: Purpose, meaning and motivation
themes.about: What Luthier is for and why to build it: recovering meaning under AI, platforms, epistemics, biology.

themes.name: Dependent types and the HoTT foundation
themes.about: Which type-theoretic foundation Luthier maps onto and what it provides.

themes.name: Luthier as a higher-order cross-language orchestrator
themes.about: A minimal bridge-language butler that coordinates other languages and their programs.

themes.name: Equality: definitional, propositional and levels
themes.about: The distinct equalities and the levels of equivalence the language expresses.

themes.name: Constructors, recursors and data mechanics
themes.about: How data declarations give types, constructors and recursors, and how match derives from them.

themes.name: Declaration versus definition and the states of a type
themes.about: Declared, defined, determined, certified; whether type and value are one scale.

themes.name: Objects as cyclic codependent definitions
themes.about: Interdependent laws making a group of types one object, a cycle in the definition graph.

themes.name: The code universe and reflection
themes.about: A closed Tarski universe of codes so generators and generic functors can be written in Luthier.

themes.name: What Luthier is for: expressiveness, minimalism and its limits
themes.about: Whether it adds real expressiveness, stays legible, is worth its cost, and where it begins to be useful.

themes.name: The declarative/executive split and realization
themes.about: Separating the timeless plan from execution, the host as a realization, and writing the interpreter in Luthier.

themes.name: Arrays and performance primitives
themes.about: Vec and Mat as definitions whose fast implementations are externs certified against them.

themes.name: Early identifier and naming explorations
themes.about: The 2022 ideas on identifiers as the human-machine dictionary and on names for dynamic objects.

themes.name: Decorators, uncertainty functors and value annotations
themes.about: Decorating a value with error, provenance or what is known about it, and the views one can take.
